dossier.public_summary: The 11-day dip changes by more than an order of magnitude between sectors and even flips to negative within the same pipeline, and individual transits range from ~15 to ~1955 ppm. Such transit-to-transit and sector-to-sector swings are not seen for a real planet and match the star's own spot variability plus folding artefacts. With no stable depth on target, the blend is rejected as a planet.

reasons.why: Depth varies by orders of magnitude within the same SPOC 2-min product, e.g. sector 18 1687±158 ppm vs sector 40 -7±56 ppm, sector 15 -141±46 ppm vs sector 18 1687±158 ppm. A true transit on the target must be consistent within one source; this pattern is spot/detrending or a blended variable, not a planet.

Individual transits are wildly inconsistent, with a few very deep events driving the Fourier signal. Top 3 carry 0.639 of the signal; a consistent planet shows small transit-to-transit scatter, not this.

reasons.why: Sector-to-sector depth changes far beyond calibration, including negative measured depths, as seen per-sector list with many -50 to -183 ppm measurements. This positively favours systematics / blended folded variability over a planetary transit.

Marginal second dip at ~0.71 phase with depth ~30% of primary equals the best apparent brightening, consistent with spot modulation in this VARIABLE (V) K dwarf rather than a hot-planet occultation. Combined with shape v_sigma -0.2124, not flat-bottom exclusion.

No on-target centroid to confirm, but no close pixel-scale neighbour requiring blend. The variable-depth pattern is best explained by stellar variability/spots on target or resolved blended variable, not a planet. RUWE 1.506 supports variability binary, xgboost planet_rank 0.17 agrees.
